learn: Hardware is the parts of a computer you can touch: the screen, keyboard, mouse and the chips inside.
Phones, tablets, laptops and game consoles all have hardware.
If hardware breaks, it may need to be repaired or replaced.
lessons.try: List five pieces of hardware in your home or classroom.

learn: Software is the programs that tell hardware what to do.
Apps, games and web browsers are software.
Software can be updated to fix bugs and add features.
lessons.try: Name three apps you have used and what each one does.

learn: Hardware needs software to do anything useful. Software needs hardware to run on.
A camera app (software) uses the camera (hardware) to take photos.
Together they make a computing system.
check: Hardware and software together make a...
lessons.try: Pick an app and name the hardware it uses.

learn: Apps are programs on phones and tablets.
A drawing app, a reading app and a game are all software.
You cannot touch software, but you can use it.
lessons.try: List four apps you have used.

learn: The operating system runs the whole computer.
It starts apps and manages files.
It is the first software to start.
check: It is the ___ software to start.
lessons.try: Watch a tablet start and spot when the operating system appears.

learn: Storage keeps files even when the computer is off.
Memory holds what the computer is doing right now.
Saving puts work in storage.
check: Files stay in ___ when the computer is off.

lessons.try: Save a drawing, turn off, and open it again.

learn: Describe the problem: "The app froze."

Use a typing app to write.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Hardware and Software
learn: Hardware: touchable parts.
Software: programs.

learn: Keep your fingers on the home row and reach for other keys.

learn: A file is saved work, like a story or a drawing.
Give files a clear name so you can find them later, like my-dog-story.
Save often so you do not lose work.

Put art in an Art folder and stories in a Stories folder.
Organized folders make work easy to find.

"Bird Drawing" is better than "Thing".
Good names help you find work later.

Good names make search easy.

learn: An algorithm is a step-by-step plan to solve a problem.

learn: A big task can be broken into smaller parts. This is called decomposition.
Cleaning your room: pick up toys, put away clothes, make the bed.
Small parts are easier to solve.
check: Breaking a big task into small parts is...
Making the bed is a small part of...
lessons.try: Break planning a party into five small tasks.

learn: Two algorithms can solve the same problem.
One might take fewer steps. That one is more efficient.
Clear and short is often best.
check: Fewer steps for the same job
Can two algorithms solve the same problem?

learn: "Make breakfast" is a big step.
Break it into small steps: get bowl, pour cereal, add milk.
Small steps are easier to follow.
check: Breaking a big job into small parts is...
lessons.try: Break "get ready for school" into small steps.

learn: "Draw a circle. Draw two dots inside."

Compare pictures after.

Choices make algorithms smarter.

Loops make programs shorter and easier to read.

All the steps inside repeat together.

Games use forever loops to keep checking for key presses.
A blinking light uses a forever loop: on, wait, off, wait.

A loop holds a group of steps.

A triangle: repeat 3 (move, turn).

Circle them.
Replace them with a loop.
check: Steps that repeat can become a...

Touching a coin makes a sound and adds a point.

Every program needs a start.
Put it at the top.

Then the other answers.

check: The second sprite ___ after the first.

learn: When the bell rings, we line up.
When the light turns green, cars go.

learn: Click, key, start events.

Events everywhere.

learn: Data is facts and numbers we collect.

Compare the numbers: most, least, how many more.
Computers can make graphs from data quickly.

"Which fruit: apple, banana or orange?"
Clear choices make counting easy.

learn: Some websites are made for kids and are safe. Others are not.

If something pops up asking you to click, ask a grown-up first.

Never agree to meet someone you only know online.
Do not share photos or private details with strangers.

Leave and tell if a chat feels wrong.
check: In game chats, never share your...

learn: Downloads can bring bad software.
Ask a grown-up before downloading.
Only use trusted stores.

Never post mean comments.
check: A kind comment includes something you...

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Internet Safety
learn: Safe sites and searches.
No strangers, no secrets.
